Route 1: Thermal Decomposition method for PEG coated Fe3O4

1. Prepare the reaction mixture by combining iron(III) acetylacetonate (Fe(acac)3, 2.0 g) with oleic acid (6.0 mL) and 11-aminoundecanoic acid tetramethylammonium salt (11-AATS, 0.5 g) as surface-directing additives in trioctylamine (30 mL) as the high-boiling solvent. Add polyethylene glycol (PEG-2000, 1.5 g) to serve as the coating agent.

2. Heat the mixture under nitrogen atmosphere with continuous stirring, gradually increasing the temperature to 120°C and maintaining for 30 minutes to remove moisture and low-boiling impurities.

3. Further increase the temperature to 320°C at a controlled heating rate of 3°C/min and maintain at reflux for 60 minutes to allow complete thermal decomposition of the iron precursor and nucleation/growth of Fe3O4 nanoparticles.

4. Allow the reaction mixture to cool naturally to room temperature under inert atmosphere. Add ethanol (50 mL) to precipitate the PEG-coated nanoparticles.

5. Collect the product by magnetic separation or centrifugation, wash three times with ethanol and hexane mixture to remove excess surfactants, and dry under vacuum at 60°C overnight.

Final product: PEG coated Fe3O4 as spherical nanoparticles with a cubic (inverse spinel) crystal structure, particle size approximately 120 nm × 120 nm × 120 nm, matching PDF reference 19-0629 (magnetite).
